From: Jordan Price <jordan.price@brightleaf.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: Brightleaf Security <security@brightleaf.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: CAIQ / field ownership question for OneTrust + Vendr sync

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. As we start to map our questionnaire exports into your vendor portal, a couple of things have come up on our side:

- The CAIQ output from our tooling lists several "field types" (e.g., data_residency.primary_region, admin_contact.email) that we treat differently than the OneTrust QnA rows.
- In Vendr we currently have duplicate fields for "Incident contact" (webhook URL vs email) and we'd like Redwood to display a single canonical field to downstream reviewers.

Would Redwood be open to a short sprint to:
1) agree a canonical field map (CAIQ -> OneTrust QnA -> Vendr field id)
2) assign an internal owner for each canonical field (Redwood vs customer) so future evidence uploads align with the right place
3) define TTL/retention for temporary credentials referenced in proofs so our auditors don't chase stale artifacts

I've attached the CAIQ_field_map_v1.xlsx and a OneTrust export to illustrate. We're flexible on timeline but would like something in place before our audit kickoff on Sep 10.

Cheers,
Jordan
Jordan Price
Security Operations, Brightleaf

Thanks Kimberly. I pulled the attached workbook and sketched an initial canonicalization approach. Notes:

- I collapsed similar CAIQ nodes into a single canonical namespace (e.g., caiq.networking.firewall.rules -> caiq.networking.firewall).
- For duplicate vendor fields (Incident contact webhook vs email) I propose a portal-level alias where both source fields map to "incident.contact" and the portal UI shows the preferred display value (email) with an expand control to view raw source values.
- Ownership: default to "customer" for contact/info fields, "redwood" for runtime/ingress controls we manage. We'll include an override flag for SOC2 customer-managed attestations.
- TTLs: default 30d for ephemeral creds, 365d for long-lived artifacts; we'll add a metadata tag so auditors can filter by "proof_retention".

Action items I can take this week:
- Convert the workbook into a machine-readable CSV + add a sample mapping script (Python) for the pipeline.
- Draft the one-pager playbook for upload and ownership handoff.

Questions for Ben: can the portal store both a canonical key + a list of source field ids? The UX requirement is to show the canonical value by default and allow reviewers to see source provenance. Also will need an API to push ownership flags from our support console.

I'll target EOD Tue (Aug 24) for the draft.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Lead, Platform Trust & Onboarding, Redwood Inference

All — quick reply from infra/dev side. We can store a canonical key and an ordered list of source ids per profile entry; backend change is small (schema: canonical_key, source_ids[], owner_flag, retention_days). UX details: should be straightforward to surface canonical vs source values; I'll add an "expand provenance" affordance. Estimated sprint: 4 dev days + 2 QA days if we don't need migration of historical data; +3 days if we have to migrate older profiles into canonical keys.

Edge cases we should call out:
- Binary attachments referenced by a QnA answer need an immutable pointer (S3 signed URL) with expiry; we'll enforce our TTL metadata on those pointers.
- For accounts that expect Redwood to manage evidence, set owner_flag=redwood and we auto-provision a signed bucket link.

Happy to sync on Wed 25th for 30m to confirm scope.

Ben Carter
